front.title: Evidence-Bounded Authorization for Agentic Systems: Evidence Qualification Receipts

abstract.t: Autonomous agents increasingly make or propose consequential actions using premises assembled from model outputs, memory, tools, telemetry, and external data. Existing authentication and authorization mechanisms can establish who is acting, under whose delegation, and which operation is permitted, but they do not by themselves establish whether the proposition that triggered the operation has adequate support. This document defines the Evidence Qualification Receipt (EQR), a transport-neutral JSON data model and fail-closed verification procedure for binding a proposition to a declared evidence profile, its supporting evidence digests, contradiction state, freshness, and evaluation result. An EQR can be PASS, FAIL, or INDETERMINATE. A PASS EQR is only an authorization input: it is never itself permission to execute. The design is append-only: changed evidence produces a successor receipt rather than rewriting prior epistemic state. The goal is to prevent evidence, provenance, or model confidence from silently acquiring authorization semantics.
